Latin word

ipsa

pronoun, intensive: feminine of ipse · Wiktionary

herself (for emphasis: she herself, of her own accord)

In this lexicon

  • herself

    the recommended word · classical · Mart. 13.23.2: ipsa merum sēcum portat et ipsa salem; Phaedr. 1.26.7–12: satiātur ipsa

Examples

  • Chīa senī similis Bacchō, quem Sētia mīsit, ipsa merum sēcum portat et ipsa salem

    Chian figs: like old Bacchus, whom Setia sent, she brings her own neat wine with her, and her own salt.Mart. 13.23.1–2

    In the entry for herself

  • quae vulpem cum revocāsset, intrītō cibō plēnam lagōnam posuit: huic rōstrum īnserēns satiātur ipsa et torquet convīvam famē. quae cum lagōnae collum frūstrā lamberet, peregrīnam sīc locūtam volucrem accēpimus: sua quisque exempla dēbet aequō animō patī

    Inviting the fox in her turn, she set before her a flask full of minced food; thrusting her beak into it, she ate her fill herself and tormented her guest with hunger. When the fox licked the neck of the flask in vain, the bird is said to have spoken thus: “Everyone should bear with good grace the example he has set.”Phaedr. 1.26.7–12

    In the entry for herself

  • ego ipsa sum, inquit, hīc hospita

    “I’m only a guest here myself,” she said.Cic. Att. 5.1.3
